clauses.reason: An immutable batch base strands every open batch once a sibling delivers, and reopening loses all admissions and conflict resolutions.

updates.rationale: Delivery publishes onto the exact recorded base, so a batch whose base cannot move is discarded after any sibling delivery, losing every admission and resolution. A merge keeps committed admission history intact, unlike a rebase, and advancing the base only along delivered descendants keeps the record a single authority that commit history can confirm. Re-admitting members would only repeat evidence already bound to their exact tips; final still runs its complete gate on the new base.
updates.statement: Batch creation records the fresh delivery tip as the batch base without executing its obsolete environment. That base changes only when maintenance workspace-sync in the batch merges a newer delivery tip that descends from it; the merge commit carries Signetum-Batch-Sync and Signetum-Batch-Base for the new base, and a conflict completes through batch-continue before the base advances. Admitted members stay admitted and their admission provenance stays bound to the base in effect when they were merged. Named qualified members must declare prepare and batch gates; after admission or synchronization, the existing owner prepares and runs the batch gate over the commits added since its last pass. Member opening still prepares its approved source.

clauses.reason: Two members claimed TOOL-OBJECT-005 concurrently and nothing refused until the decision history projection.

updates.rationale: Concurrent writes to one clause cannot both replay, and the projection reports that only after the work is integrated. Comparing committed contract identities at the merge points is cheap and local; automatic renumbering would rewrite approved contracts without review.
updates.statement: Batch admission and batch synchronization read the decision clause identities each change record writes in its contract decisions since the relevant base. When two different changes write one identity, the operation refuses before merging and names the clause, both changes and the workspaces that own them. Renumbering stays with the people and agents who own the changes.

decisions.reason: The owner directed that an open batch take a sibling's delivery as a merge without re-admitting its members, and that concurrent clause identities be refused at admission and synchronization.

transaction.reason: Apply the owner-approved batch synchronization and clause claim decisions
